title: Côte d'Ivoire Partners EBRD to Advance National AI Strategy
summary: Côte d'Ivoire and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development launch partnership to develop national AI strategy, infrastructure, and talent.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Côte d'Ivoire and EBRD officially launched a partnership on November 27, 2026 to develop comprehensive national AI strategy and infrastructure.
- The collaboration focuses on policy frameworks, digital infrastructure investment, and talent development across government and private sectors.
- This marks West Africa's latest push to establish regional AI leadership through international development bank partnerships and strategic planning.


Côte d'Ivoire has entered a strategic partnership with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to design and implement a comprehensive national artificial intelligence strategy. Officially launched on November 27, 2026, the collaboration aims to position the West African nation as a regional leader in AI adoption, digital infrastructure, and technology-driven economic development.


## Partnership Scope and Objectives


The EBRD partnership centers on three core pillars: policy framework development, infrastructure investment, and human capital formation. Côte d'Ivoire's government will work with EBRD technical advisors to draft regulatory guidelines for AI deployment across public services, healthcare, agriculture, and financial sectors. The framework includes data governance standards, ethical AI principles, and cross-border collaboration protocols aligned with African Union digital transformation initiatives.


Infrastructure development represents a critical component of the strategy. The EBRD will provide technical assistance and potential financing mechanisms to expand broadband connectivity, establish data centers, and upgrade government digital systems. These investments target rural regions where connectivity gaps currently limit technology access and economic opportunity.


## Release Date and Implementation Timeline


Officially launched on November 27, 2026, the partnership follows an 18-month scoping phase that began in mid-2025. The national AI strategy document is expected to reach completion by Q2 2027, with initial pilot programs launching in select ministries and regional hubs by late 2027. Full implementation across government agencies and private sector partnerships is targeted for 2028-2030.


## Regional Context and Competitive Positioning


This announcement follows similar national AI initiatives across Africa, including partnerships between[OpenAI and Chile for national AI adoption](https://emergent.sh/news/openai-partners-chile-national-ai-adoption) and[Australia's collaboration with MIT to accelerate AI adoption](https://emergent.sh/news/australia-partners-mit-accelerate-ai-adoption) . Côte d'Ivoire's approach emphasizes public-private partnerships and regional coordination within the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) framework.


The EBRD brings expertise from similar technology strategy projects in emerging markets across Europe, Central Asia, and North Africa. The bank's involvement signals growing international development finance interest in African AI capacity building, particularly in countries demonstrating political stability and economic reform momentum.


## Talent Development and Skills Programs


The partnership includes commitments to establish AI training programs at Ivorian universities and technical institutes. The EBRD will facilitate knowledge transfer partnerships with European research institutions and technology companies. Initial programs target 5,000 students and mid-career professionals over three years, with specialized tracks in machine learning engineering, data science, and AI ethics.


Government officials emphasized the importance of retaining local talent and creating domestic technology employment opportunities. The strategy includes incentives for Ivorian diaspora technologists to return and participate in national AI development efforts.


## What This Means


Côte d'Ivoire's partnership with the EBRD represents a structured approach to national AI readiness that balances infrastructure investment, regulatory preparation, and human capital development. By engaging an established development finance institution, the government demonstrates commitment to evidence-based policy frameworks and international best practices. The success of this initiative could serve as a replicable model for other West African nations seeking to build AI capacity through multilateral partnerships rather than purely commercial vendor relationships. The 2027-2030 implementation timeline provides a realistic roadmap for sustainable technology adoption aligned with broader economic development goals.
